title: 1972 AHSME Problem 5
statement: From among \(2^{\frac{1}{2}},\) \(3^{\frac{1}{3}},\) \(8^{\frac{1}{8}},\) \(9^{\frac{1}{9}},\) those which have the greatest and the next to the greatest values, in that order, are:

solutions.text:
Raising to convenient common powers gives \[ (3^{\frac{1}{3}})^6=9>8=(2^{\frac{1}{2}})^6, \] \[ (2^{\frac{1}{2}})^8=16>8=(8^{\frac{1}{8}})^8, \] and \[ (2^{\frac{1}{2}})^{18}=512>81=(9^{\frac{1}{9}})^{18}. \] Thus \(3^{\frac{1}{3}}\) is greatest and \(2^{\frac{1}{2}}\) is next.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Compare two roots by raising both positive numbers to a common power
First compare \(3^{\frac{1}{3}}\) with \(2^{\frac{1}{2}}\), then compare \(2^{\frac{1}{2}}\) with each remaining number
